intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream replaces the orchestration ledger CLI with native workers, project notes, PR/CI subscriptions, owner-only branch writes, and a different-family verifier for every PR. It removes all orch scripts and tests, and assumes Task cloud workers and built-state forks.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp removes the obsolete CLI and test targets, adopts the shorter owner-per-PR playbook, and keeps pstack_start_agent, native result delivery and scoped follow-ups, read-only liveness checks, and explicit file transfer rather than assuming a fork copies runtime state. Project notes use the agreed store or workspace-local files. Replacements require terminal ownership reconciliation; the pilot and every shared write remain within explicit authorization. Earlier ledger and stacker-specific departures are superseded by this owner-per-PR workflow. The plugin's separate runtime ownership journal is unchanged.
intentionalDepartures.why: Adopt upstream's simpler coordination without inventing Amp APIs, losing a live child's ownership, or treating a verifier's approval as permission to publish or merge.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream rewrites statechart as a TypeScript compiler, requires run-proven interrogate findings, uses a different-family arena judge, simplifies autopilot-stack, and adds catch-up subtitles and premeasurement decisions.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp adopts the new CLI and documents removed commands; keeps its Bash entrypoint and Node-only test discovery, locked test dependencies, JDK setup and strict compiler typecheck. A return-type annotation and two test callback return fixes satisfy strict checking. Renderer-test installs disable lifecycle scripts. Numeric TLC messages supersede runtime heading patches; both headings have regression coverage, and the plain-TLC test oracle retains TLC 1.8 named-heading compatibility. Earlier statechart runtime departures are superseded where the new compiler replaces them. Interrogate reviewers keep strict read-only tools: they propose repros and the parent runs them on disposable exact-state copies, reporting blocked repros as unverified. Arena keeps its mandatory judge gate and fails when a known parent has no known different-family seat; it never guesses a fallback or rewrites configuration. Autopilot-stack inherits full without merging, with dependent-only stacks and owner-only rebases. Amp schedules, explicit shared-write permissions, qualified skills, native visuals, and silent catch-up video remain intact.
intentionalDepartures.why: Adopt the new behavior without weakening Amp role capabilities, permission boundaries, test coverage, or user model customizations. Models prove only their stated bounds; executable view modules and toolchain installs must be explicit.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream splits statechart into modules, adds temporal-loop reporting and real PNG tests, and snapshots input files before TLC runs.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp retains the Node wrapper and renamed Node suite, extends TLC 1.8 temporal-heading compatibility to property-loop.mjs, resolves Java to an absolute path in tests and gives fake mise installations a tla2tools.jar symlink for versioned jars. Upstream's snapshot and fingerprint barriers replace the earlier custom concurrent-edit wait. Setup checks Node crc32 support, installs renderer test fonts, and prewarms pinned Pele/resvg so missing dependencies fail setup instead of skipping rendering coverage.
intentionalDepartures.why: Preserve TLC compatibility and reproducible tests without retaining superseded concurrency scaffolding. Real rendering and font checks must run in fresh orbs and CI.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds ketchup-video, broadens statechart to any system with a Pele renderer, routes model-check results through statechart, fixes PR discovery and polling, and moves reflect edits out of plugin caches.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp keeps qualified skill routing, Node execution and TLC compatibility. Ketchup-video inherits Amp's authored-message window and read-only scope except for reply media, uses the available video workflow, and stores final media in .amp/in/artifacts. Reflect names the writable source or approved project-local copy before edits; publication needs separate authorization. Formal verification refers to pstack:statechart by name. Existing Amp thread-search worktree auditing already avoids stat/date transcript parsing, so the upstream GNU stat fix does not apply. Claude Code marketplace auto-update instructions remain outside this Amp port.
intentionalDepartures.why: Preserve Amp's source-of-truth repositories, permissions, transcript APIs, and artifact conventions while adopting upstream behavior. Renderer and toolchain downloads are disclosed, and model evidence is not proof of product correctness.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds statechart, its Node.js chart/TLA+ tools, fixtures, output-folder model, and tests.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp registers the qualified skill with permission, disposable-output, executable-mapping and native-diagram guidance. A Bash entrypoint preserves Node semantics. Upstream tests are named statechart.node.mjs to avoid Bun discovery and run under node --test via test:statechart; their concurrent-edit test waits for TLC's initial-state output instead of a fixed 500 ms delay. Setup installs Java and checksum-pinned TLC 1.7.4 for integration coverage. The TLC parser and tests accept both the old plural and TLC 1.8 named temporal-property violation messages.
intentionalDepartures.why: Bun differs from Node in NODE_OPTIONS and exception formatting. Preserve Node execution rather than weakening error-path tests. Java can start after the old test delay, so the edit must wait until it has read the first spec. TLC 1.8's valid counterexamples must not be mistaken for tool failures. Generated model evidence does not establish real-product correctness or authorize shared writes.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream changes sharpen from executing a task to returning a rewritten prompt, with four explicit checks for expertise, raw material, methods and outside evidence.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp adopts the prompt-only workflow and matching guide and help text, retains qualified named-only invocation and explicit user constraints, and states the no-execution boundary in the skill itself.
intentionalDepartures.why: The rewritten prompt is the deliverable, not permission to perform the task. Amp permission boundaries and the user's choices remain authoritative.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds formal-verification maintenance, coverage and sync-commit records, real-code generated-input fallback, an optional setup offer, and guide and sharpen updates.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp registers maintenance with qualified invocation and building-skills, keeps scratch variants isolated from user changes, preserves no-product-fix and blocked-sync rules, and adopts the optional offer and applicable guide additions. Help checks for existing verification rather than assuming that an absent skill proves no verifier exists. Sharpen retains explicit user constraints. Claude Code installation guidance remains outside the Amp guide.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp's skill, permission and model configuration boundaries remain authoritative. A proof's coverage must not be inferred from a filename, and a maintenance run must not overwrite existing work or hide a product bug.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds create-formal-verification-skill, makes ketchup list every pending item with evidence and risk instead of imposing a total word cap, validates TypeScript brands with type guards, and updates harness and guide prose.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp registers the new skill with named or coordinator-routed invocation, building-skills and project-local output. Ketchup retains read-only transcript pagination, multiplayer attribution and native visuals while adopting item-scaled replies. TypeScript guidance and applicable guide corrections port directly; existing Amp-specific guide summaries remain. Claude Code model-rule and skip-feature mappings remain excluded, and already normalized skill names need no change.
intentionalDepartures.why: Formal verification must preserve its stated bounds, counterexamples and no-product-fix contract. Host-specific model, permission and tool mappings must not replace Amp's native behavior.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds Claude Code installation and generated-harness instructions, a Cursor-to-Claude tool/model/path adapter, and a clarification that Benny uses Cursor Automations.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp retains its own installation instructions and native adapter. The Claude Code harness documentation and generator instructions are not copied into this plugin.
intentionalDepartures.why: Those mappings target a different host. Applying them in Amp would replace native roles, model configuration and thread execution with unsupported Claude Code conventions. Benny remains omitted as recorded in benny-removed.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream makes ketchup explanatory and picture-led, excludes visuals from its word budget, and refines premise testing, legitimate-state guards, behavioral tests and crash reconciliation while trimming repeated guidance.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp adopts those changes and the shorter principle and review prose. Ketchup retains read-only, paginated transcript and multiplayer boundaries, uses plain diagrams or creating-views rather than Mermaid by default, and keeps tables inside the text budget. Native role ownership and permission rules remain intact.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp transcript APIs, visual conventions and authorization boundaries differ from Cursor; existing user model customizations remain independent of this prose-only sync.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds per-spawn Cursor effort/fast slug adjustments and composer panel-family recognition, sharpen, shorter ketchup, and simplified autopilot and shipping protocols.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp keeps configured role and panel models, effort and speed with no per-call overrides or guessed model fallback; the coordinator explains that boundary instead of repeating unavailable knobs in every workflow. Sharpen uses qualified explicit invocation and retains user constraints. Ketchup uses small plain diagrams or creating-views, a total 150-word budget and two-line decisions. Autopilot adopts swarm-once and merge-result checks but retains terminal-before-replacement, explicit shared-write authorization, native schedules, and root-owned transferred trails. Stack and Shipping retain their detailed step structure and event-wake/watch safety while adopting sole topology ownership, no writes during landing, fresh independent verdicts and Origin's plain merge command.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp role tools expose no per-spawn effort or speed fields, and its configured panels already preserve model diversity. Native APIs, permissions, ownership and evidence requirements remain authoritative.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream removes Cursor mode/reminder flags, asks delegates to find a hidden poteto-mode skill by absolute path or highest-version Cursor plugin, and makes ketchup picture-led with Mermaid and /visualize.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp keeps its native registered mode and qualified skill loading, including hybrid inline worker contracts, rather than adding Cursor discovery paths or passing the coordinator to every worker. Ketchup adopts the word limit, factual state visual, number checks and three-line decisions, but uses plain-text diagrams or Amp creating-views and reports missing evidence rather than fabricating it. The new in-your-own-words skill is explicitly invoked through its qualified Amp name.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp skills are not hidden behind Cursor's catalog flag; its mode API, strict worker capabilities, visual tools and permission boundaries differ.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream adds an agent-plugins.org manifest, removes redundant exploration and babysit prose, prints the worktree audit base before its stdout table, and asks ketchup to prefer Mermaid or generated images.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp retains native index.ts registration rather than adding a foreign manifest; keeps a short tool-neutral explorer evidence contract and babysit's merge-authorization warning and reply requirements; reports the audit base on stderr to preserve its stdout table. Ketchup may build reply artifacts from existing evidence, uses plain-text diagrams by default, and never fabricates screens. Existing comment-reviewer role routing and the hybrid worker wrapper remain native.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp's strict explorers cannot load additional skills, audit consumers rely on the stable table header, and host rules govern visuals, approval, and routing independently of Cursor.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream ketchup catches up since the user's last message by reading the visible thread and calling a Read tool for bro.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp ketchup uses the visible conversation and paginated pstack_read_current_thread history, identifies the invoking user's authored messages rather than scheduled wake-ups or child reports, and reads the linked bro skill. It stays read-only and distinguishes unchecked live state from verified state.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp threads include scheduled and multiplayer messages and can compact earlier context; catch-up must not silently skip that history or treat automated wake-ups as the user's last instruction.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream 0.15.16 condenses workflow prose, removes some examples, and derives most principle and playbook paths from titles.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp adopts the shorter workflow and reference prose but retains explicit coordinator leaf names and playbook paths, useful public-boundary test and type examples, Linux profiler fallback, native worker contracts, checklist semantics, and explicit shared-write approval rules.
intentionalDepartures.why: Explicit names and retained examples keep routing and contracts inspectable without reintroducing Cursor APIs or weakening Amp permissions.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream 0.15.15 drops Sol from default panels and reflect tooling, and uses Opus xhigh and Grok xhigh defaults; large matches those defaults.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp retains the deliberately tuned role map in index.ts, including GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna, three-family panels, and per-role efforts. Budget selection still changes efforts without changing model IDs or panel order; unlimited selects each model's highest supported effort. Neutral reviewer and runner wording is retained where it suits configured counts. The orch test's Sol verifier label remains valid opaque data.
intentionalDepartures.why: The Amp map was deliberately customized in e88c4a4 and 642549f for model capability and cost. An upstream default change must not erase those choices or imply all Amp defaults match a single reasoning budget.

intentionalDepartures.from: Typed-only /poteto-help explains Cursor installation, Custom Modes, model rules, subagents, and /loop, and asks a multiple-choice question when the need is unclear.
intentionalDepartures.to: Explicit-only pstack:poteto-help explains the Amp directory plugin, poteto mode, resolved role map, native threads, and authorized hourly schedules. It asks a plain clarifying question unless the user explicitly requested questions, and links Amp port sources. It offers setup at most once when relevant and not known complete, without inferring setup history from missing files or a resolved map, which has no provenance metadata.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp has different installation and orchestration APIs, no disable-model-invocation flag, and restricts multiple-choice dialogs to explicit user requests. Help remains advice-only; requests for work load poteto-mode.

intentionalDepartures.from: Delegated workers can inherit broad coordinator instructions.
intentionalDepartures.to: The Poteto parent retains the full coordinator skill; worker modes receive role contracts and completed templates inline, with only applicable qualified execution skills loaded by non-strict workers.
intentionalDepartures.why: This preserves role behavior while avoiding coordinator context and capabilities in workers, especially strict read-only seats.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor's guide repeats workflows through longer examples and editor-specific instructions.
intentionalDepartures.to: The Amp guide condenses examples and links to authoritative skills and playbooks, retaining task switching, session pickup, design choices, verification, overnight audit, and skill evaluation contracts.
intentionalDepartures.why: Editorial condensation avoids repeating platform-specific instructions without changing the workflows.

intentionalDepartures.from: Upstream bundles a Slack issue-triage and reproduction automation pack.
intentionalDepartures.to: The automation pack and generic pstack wake tool are omitted; task-specific workflows use Amp's native webhook API.
intentionalDepartures.why: The user requested removal of the unused automation.

intentionalDepartures.from: **Just do it.** Use any MCP tool. Reversible work and external actions proceed without asking. Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call that the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer. Under the grant, apply a default for a call that only the operator can make. Report the default with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead. The operator answers in their own words. Never give a shorthand token to type back. Gates that the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp preserves those full-autonomy decision boundaries, but full autonomy does not authorize shared or external writes; those still require the user's explicit approval.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp permission boundaries are stricter than Cursor pstack autonomy.

intentionalDepartures.from: **Defaults for every `Task` call.** `run_in_background: true`
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp child threads with durable IDs, orbs, named runners, and schedules. Details live in references/amp-adapter.md.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp has no Cursor Task. Durable threads are the native equivalent.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor custom mode with disable-model-invocation: true
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp poteto extends builtin medium. Mode instructions are advisory and do not strip write tools or invent tool gates.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp plugin modes cannot sandbox the coordinator or enforce the playbook.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor parent uses the user's chat model
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp poteto inherits builtin medium's model, reasoning, and tools, and persists the full bundled Poteto skill in the mode instructions.
intentionalDepartures.why: This preserves Cursor Use as Mode parity while leaving parent inference routing to Amp.

intentionalDepartures.from: You can spawn a subagent even though you are one. "The app is small" and "a subagent cannot spawn one" are both wrong.
intentionalDepartures.to: Feature keeps the Amp sentence that a child can spawn a child, and that a small app is not a reason to skip delegation.
intentionalDepartures.why: 0.15.5 removed that Cursor sentence. Amp still needs it so an owner does not treat nested spawn as impossible.

intentionalDepartures.from: Ten lanes on `[^`<>]+` at the PR head
intentionalDepartures.to: The Amp checker also rejects a whitespace-only model inside the backticks.
intentionalDepartures.why: Upstream 0.15.5 and later reject angle brackets and empty ticks. A blank model is not a filled model, so the Amp checker tightens that boundary.

intentionalDepartures.from: A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits Task model. A rejected slug falls back to the same family on that Task call.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp roles resolve through the plugin. inherit-parent and auto stay invalid. A rejected single-role spawn stops. A rejected panel seat is one dropout. A replacement config write happens only when the user asks, then reload before the next orb spawn. There is no per-call model argument.
intentionalDepartures.why: pstack_start_agent and pstack_run_panel take a role or panel. modelFor and panelFor resolve the map. Orb agents are registered at plugin load.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor marks routed pstack skills disable-model-invocation: true.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp keeps the skills in its catalog but scopes their descriptions to named use or poteto-mode routing; setup-pstack remains directly discoverable.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp skill frontmatter has no equivalent catalog suppression flag, so trigger wording carries the routing boundary.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor budgets rewrite effort-bearing model slugs and allow inherit-parent or auto.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp setup reads show-agent-options capabilities and writes per-seat model and effort values, capping each concrete model to supported effort while mapping builtin budgets to builtin aliases.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp exposes effort separately from model IDs and validates per-model effort capabilities at runtime.

intentionalDepartures.from: Custom arena counts launch one Task per candidate model choice.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp passes count, capped at 20, to one pstack_run_panel call and cycles configured seats in order.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp panels own candidate labeling, run tracking, dropout handling, and cross-judge gating; arbitrary per-candidate roles do not exist.

intentionalDepartures.from: Cursor instructions invoke scripts relative to the plugin checkout and may execute shell scripts directly.
intentionalDepartures.to: Amp instructions resolve scripts from the loaded skill base and invoke them explicitly with bun or bash.
intentionalDepartures.why: A synced Amp install may run from any user working directory and does not preserve executable bits.

intentionalDepartures.from: On the operator's go, arm `/loop 1h` with a prompt that runs this tick. `/loop` works in local and cloud roots.
intentionalDepartures.to: On the operator's go, the root arms an hourly Amp schedule on its own thread (set_schedule with RRULE:FREQ=HOURLY and run_mode existing) and clears it when no delegated work is left or on the operator's stop. Ticks re-read playbooks from the loaded skill, not git show origin/main in the target repo.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp has no /loop. A schedule in run_mode existing wakes the root with its program context, survives orb pause, and only runs under the user's explicit request for ongoing work.

intentionalDepartures.from: Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs.
intentionalDepartures.to: New work goes to a fresh pstack_start_agent child with consolidated scope. A running owner is still steered with send_thread_message for its current scope. A current-checkout child holds no checkout state of its own, and download_thread_changes can move an idle orb owner's changed files to a fresh owner.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp ownership claims already forbid a second live owner, and native thread file transfer makes orb state cheaper to move than in Cursor, so reuse is rarer.

intentionalDepartures.from: When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI.
intentionalDepartures.to: Opening a PR keeps the forge-only Size and stacks and Readiness rules. The adapter records that Amp has no built-in PR tool and that ship_thread_changes is a project Ship prompt, not a PR tool.
intentionalDepartures.why: The rule protects state that a Cursor cloud agent PR tool tracks. Amp has no such tool, so the paragraph would only invite agents to look for one.

intentionalDepartures.from: Spawn a fresh `poteto-agent` for each new task, and resume one only in the strict cases that poteto-mode's Subagents section names.
intentionalDepartures.to: agents/poteto-agent.md stays a prompt resource. The fresh-children rule lives in poteto-mode Agents and threads and the adapter.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp never routes requests to a poteto-agent subagent, so a routing description there has no reader.

intentionalDepartures.from: check-plan only requires the program markers "git show origin/main:", "/loop 1h", and "status message".
intentionalDepartures.to: The Amp checker requires "loaded skill", "hourly Amp schedule", and "status message", and also rejects a program checklist that still mentions /loop, /goal, or a 30-minute cadence.
intentionalDepartures.why: An acceptance run showed a plan with both the hourly Amp schedule and leftover Cursor cadence passed. Two cadences in one plan let an agent arm the wrong one.

intentionalDepartures.from: The how explorer and explainer prompts name a Read tool and ask for mermaid diagrams.
intentionalDepartures.to: They read files with whatever read tool the role has and draw plain-text diagram blocks, using Mermaid only on request.
intentionalDepartures.why: Amp renders diagram blocks as monospaced text and its read-only roles do not expose a tool named Read.
